description:
Introduced knowingly by bedrock-z2e and documented in `do_worker_recheck/3`.

When a monitored worker dies, the `:DOWN` always arrives before the supervisor has started a replacement — the foreman is notified the instant the process dies, while the supervisor must first handle its own `EXIT`. So the foreman records `:stopped` and then rechecks on a timer, adopting the replacement when it appears.

The recheck window is bounded: `@recheck_interval_ms 25` x `@recheck_attempts 20` = 500ms in `foreman/server.ex`. A supervisor that takes longer than that — a worker whose `init/1` is slow (Shale preallocates WAL segments), or a node under heavy load — leaves the worker recorded `:stopped` while it is in fact running.

## Consequence

Stale in the safe direction: the foreman understates readiness rather than naming a dead process as running. But it is not harmless — `do_get_all_running_services/1` filters on `{:ok, _}`, so a live worker missed by the window stops being advertised to the coordinator, and `do_relay_tsl/2` stops sending it layout pushes, which is how a worker self-detects displacement. Nothing re-resolves afterwards: `start_workers_that_are_stopped/1` runs only from `do_spin_up/1`, i.e. at boot.

Materializers self-heal — `Olivine.Server` calls `Foreman.report_health/3` after startup, which settles the foreman's view. Shale never reports, so a log worker is the exposed case.

## Options

- have Shale report health on startup as Olivine does, so a restarted worker announces itself and no timer is needed
- make the foreman resolve `otp_name` at use, treating the registered name rather than a cached pid as the authority for 'is it running now'
- keep the timer but make it adaptive, or unbounded with a long interval

The first is the smallest and matches an existing pattern; the second removes the race entirely and would also close bedrock-z2e's residual staleness, at the cost of a lookup per use.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Start a worker whose replacement takes longer than the recheck window to register, kill it, and assert the foreman eventually reports it running again rather than remaining `:stopped`.
title: Foreman recheck window can miss a slow supervisor restart, leaving a live worker recorded as stopped
